page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-12 is a graphics-optimized server featuring a dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor providing 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 48.0 GB, maintaining a 4.0 GB per core ratio. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance split between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations score in the average range. Conversely, the server achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks for small (135M) and medium (7B) models, delivering high token-per-second processing and generation speeds. Large (70B) model prompt processing falls back to average.

From a resource density perspective, the g2-standard-12 offers a qualitative entry point for GPU-accelerated computing, pairing a single L4 accelerator with a balanced mid-range CPU and memory configuration. The primary tradeoff is the weak single-core CPU execution speed and the complete absence of local storage, which requires external block storage attachment. This server is best fit for small-to-medium LLM inference, graphics rendering, and GPU-accelerated machine learning workloads that do not demand high single-threaded CPU throughput.
